declaration.goal: Move ahead by about 0.45 m and stop there, keeping the heading within 12 degrees of the start heading.
declaration.measured_by: Computed from the simulator's pose, as the quantities a camera straight above could measure; not measured from a camera image. The camera sees a floor area of 2.59 m by 1.46 m. x, y and heading are relative to the start of each trial: x in the direction the body faces at the start, y to its left, heading counter-clockwise seen from above, in (-180, 180]. At the start the body is at x = 0, y = 0, and the view spans x from -0.84 to 1.74 m and y from -0.73 to 0.73 m. A value is lost when the camera could not see the tracked point.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c0 is held at 0.5 for the first 1.0 s and c1 to c4 are 0, THE system SHALL end with x between 0.1 and 1.0 m and heading within 20 degrees of 0.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Channel c0 drives the body forward

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Channel c0 drives the body forward

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: x ended near 0 for c0 (4.9e-5 m), c1 (-0.023 m) and c2 (0.0007 m). c0 and c2 at 0.5 for 1 s did nothing measurable. c1 gave a 4.4 degree turn and no forward motion. Motion stops when the input stops (about 1 s). Forward drive is not c0 at this level; c3, c4 or higher levels are untested.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c3 is held at 1.0 for the first 1.0 s and all other channels are 0, THE system SHALL end with x between 0.1 and 1.0 m.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Channel c3 or c4 drives the body forward

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Channel c3 or c4 drives the body forward

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: c3 at 1.0 for 1 s gave x 0.006 m and heading 5.2 deg. c4 gave x 0.001 m and heading -0.6 deg. c0 at 1.0 gave x about 0. No channel produced forward travel with a constant 1 s pulse. The picture shows a small body that stays in place. Constant inputs only cause small posture twitches, so forward travel may need oscillating input.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN one channel is driven by a 2 Hz sine of amplitude 1.0 for the whole trial and the others are 0, THE system SHALL end with x between 0.1 and 2.0 m for at least one of c0, c2 and c4.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: An oscillating channel produces forward travel

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: An oscillating channel produces forward travel

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Prediction x in [0.1, 2.0] failed for all three. A 2 Hz sine for 5 s gave x 0.0001 m (c0), 0.059 m with heading +22.9 deg (c2), and 0.025 m with heading -7.1 deg (c4). Oscillation moves the body more than constant pulses do, and c2 is the strongest channel, but the travel is far below 0.45 m and the heading drifts.

statement.author: dr-kiro
statement.text: WHEN c2 is driven by an 8 Hz sine of amplitude 1.0 for the whole trial, THE system SHALL end with x between 0.15 and 1.0 m.

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Higher frequency on c2 gives more forward travel

title.author: dr-kiro
title.text: Higher frequency on c2 gives more forward travel

words.author: dr-kiro
words.text: Predicted x in [0.15, 1.0] at 8 Hz on c2. The 8 Hz trial gave x -0.002 m and heading -16.4 deg. 4 Hz gave x -0.071 m and heading -62 deg. 1 Hz gave x 0.018 m and heading 0.5 deg. Higher frequency did not give more forward travel and made the body turn. The budget is used up and no trial reached 0.45 m, so the last trial (x 0.018 m, heading 0.5 deg) does not meet the goal.
